mechanism_narrative: The continuing recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the next four weeks will raise weekday foot traffic near stores, lifting RETAIL_REC relative to the prior four weeks because more commuters pass through retail corridors on work trips.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -56.3 to -37.3 across four weeks while TRANSIT improved from -61.1 to -44.3
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue improving for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior-four-week mean, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated above 10 points while WORKPLACES remains deeply negative, people will substitute toward neighborhood shopping and short errands, pushing RETAIL_REC higher within two weeks despite weak commuting.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains > 10 points while WORKPLACES stays below -30 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 14.9 and WORKPLACES was -37.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above 10 and WORKPLACES stays below -30 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not rise over that horizon, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A continued weekly rise in PARKS mobility signals warmer outdoor conditions and broader discretionary movement, which should spill over into retail-and-recreation visits and raise RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS moved from -20.9 to 19.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS keeps rising or remains positive for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve, the seasonal spillover claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: A discrete recovery in TRANSIT from very depressed levels acts as a threshold signal for reopening compliance; once TRANSIT is above -45, retail access and shopping trips should accelerate, increasing RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -45 points and remains there for at least 2 weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -44.3 at t-0w after four weeks of improvement
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays above -45 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve versus the last four weeks, this threshold mechanism is false.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of lower WORKPLACES absence and higher GROCERY_PHARM trips indicates broader out-of-home activity and essential-errand chaining; together they should support a modest increase in RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -56.3 to -37.3 while GROCERY_PHARM improved from -26.4 to -10.0
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and GROCERY_PHARM both improve for two weeks but RETAIL_REC fails to rise, the interaction is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains near baseline while RETAIL_REC is still far below baseline, consumers are already leaving home for necessities and are likely to add discretionary retail trips over the next four weeks, raising RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM is above -15 while RETAIL_REC remains below -35
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was -10.0 and RETAIL_REC was -37.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays above -15 but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over four weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, a renewed drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES should precede lower retail mobility because reduced commuting directly suppresses shopping trips during the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 5 points week-on-week or WORKPLACES falls by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT or WORKPLACES falls by more than 5 points in a week but RETAIL_REC does not fall within the next week, reject the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS together with falling RESIDENTIAL time indicates people are spending more time outside the home for leisure, which should draw retail-and-recreation mobility higher over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -20.9 to 19.3 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 24.6 to 14.9
failure_condition: If PARKS keeps rising while RESIDENTIAL falls for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its previous four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.
